name: NCP1653ADR2G
title: NCP1653, NCP1653A: fixed-frequency CCM boost PFC controller
summary: An 8-pin controller for continuous conduction mode power factor correction boost stages, switching at a fixed 100 kHz (NCP1653) or 67 kHz (NCP1653A) and driving an external MOSFET directly at up to ±1.5 A. Output voltage and line voltage are sensed as currents into FB and In, and the inductor current as a current out of CS, so few external parts are needed. It runs in average or peak current mode and with either a constant output or a follower-boost output that falls at low line or high load. Protection covers output overvoltage (107%), undervoltage/shutdown (8%), programmable overcurrent and overpower, VCC UVLO and thermal shutdown. NCP1653ADR2G is the 67 kHz part in SO-8 on tape and reel.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback / shutdown (FB/SD). Takes a current IFB, set by a resistor RFB from the PFC output, that stands for the output voltage. IFB drives output regulation, overvoltage protection and undervoltage protection: above 107% of Iref the driver is turned off (OVP); below 8% of Iref the chip goes into a low-current shutdown state.

pins.name: Vcontrol
pins.function: Control voltage / soft-start. Its voltage sets the stage's input impedance and so the power factor. A capacitor Ccontrol to ground holds the control bandwidth to about 20 Hz or less so the power factor approaches one. With Vcontrol at 0 V there is no drive, so the same capacitor gives a soft start.

pins.name: In
pins.function: Input voltage sense. Sinks a current Ivac proportional to the RMS line voltage Vac, used for duty-cycle modulation and overpower limitation. When IS·Ivac exceeds 3 nA², OPL pulls Vcontrol down indirectly and the drive duty ratio falls, cutting input power.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Input current sense. Sources a current IS that tracks the inductor current IL, used for duty-cycle modulation, overpower limitation and overcurrent protection. Above 200 µA the driver is turned off (OCP).

pins.name: VM
pins.function: Multiplier voltage. Carries the voltage VM that sets the PFC duty cycle. A resistor RM to ground sets the input impedance, which is proportional to RM. With a capacitor CM also fitted the chip runs in average current mode; without it, in peak current mode.

pins.name: Drv
pins.function: Gate drive output for the external power MOSFET.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Positive supply. Runs from 8.75 V to 18 V; the UVLO start threshold is 13.25 V.

circuits.title: Figure 1. Typical application circuit
circuits.description: A CCM boost PFC stage in outline. The line passes an EMI filter and a four-diode bridge; a small capacitor sits across the rectified bus. The boost inductor, MOSFET and diode charge the bulk capacitor at the output. The return current flows through a sense resistor between the bridge minus and ground, and a second resistor from the bridge minus feeds that information to CS as a current. A resistor from the rectified bus to In, with a capacitor to ground, gives the line-voltage current. One resistor from the output to FB sets the output level. Vcontrol has its filter capacitor, VM its resistor and capacitor, Drv drives the gate and VCC comes from a 15 V supply.

circuits.title: Figure 40. Self-biasing scheme in constant output voltage mode
circuits.description: The boost inductor carries an auxiliary winding with turns ratio n. Two diodes charge C1 and C2 from it: one to about n×Vin and the other to about n×(Vout - Vin). The two capacitors are stacked, so the voltage across them adds to n×Vout, which is steady while the output is regulated, and that stack feeds VCC through its own reservoir capacitor. VCC goes to the controller's pin 8.

parts.note: boost inductor with auxiliary winding; main winding P1-P2, auxiliary A1-A2

notes: Used in constant output voltage mode. In follower boost mode the output is not held at one level, so bias from an auxiliary inductor winding is not recommended there.

circuits.title: Figure 41. Recommended startup biasing scheme
circuits.description: Lets the PFC stage start on its own, without the second-stage converter. Three 180 kΩ resistors from the rectified input charge a 100 µF VCC capacitor. A BC556 PNP has its emitter on FB and its collector on ground; its base sits on a 1.5 MΩ / 560 kΩ divider from VCC. While VCC is low (under about 4 V) the transistor carries the FB current away to ground, so the chip draws its low no-feedback start-up current and VCC rises quickly.
notes: The values are a reference starting point.
With IFB = 0 the start-up current is at most 50 µA; with feedback current flowing and VCC under 4 V it can reach 1.5 mA.

circuits.title: Figure 42. 300 W 100 kHz power factor correction circuit
circuits.description: A complete 300 W boost PFC stage for 90 to 265 Vac input with a 390 V output, using the 100 kHz NCP1653. The line passes a fuse, a 1 µF capacitor across the line, a 150 µH series choke and a 2 × 3.9 mH common-mode choke with 680 nF across its output, then a KBU6K bridge with 100 nF across the rectified bus. A 600 µH boost inductor, SPP20N60S MOSFET and CSD04060 diode charge 100 µF 450 V. The return current passes a 0.1 Ω sense resistor (RCS) and 2.85 kΩ (RS) carries the result to CS. In senses the bus through 4.7 MΩ and 470 kΩ, with 33 nF at their joint and 1 nF at the pin. FB takes 680 k + 680 k + 560 k (1.92 MΩ) from the output with 1 nF at the pin. Ccontrol is 330 nF, RM 56 kΩ with CM 330 pF. Drv reaches the gate through 4.5 Ω with 10 kΩ gate to ground; VCC is a 15 V supply.

parts.note: common-mode choke; winding 1-2 on the line, 3-4 on the neutral

notes: With RFB = 1.92 MΩ, the 230 µA maximum OVP threshold and VFB1 = 2.5 V worst case give 444.1 V; a 450 V output capacitor is recommended for margin.

operation.text: onsemi marks the NCP1653 family as discontinued and not recommended for new designs.

A fixed-frequency boost PFC controller for continuous conduction mode, in an 8-pin package. Fixed-frequency switching at 67 kHz (NCP1653A) or 100 kHz (NCP1653, 102 kHz typ) eases meeting EMI standards, and CCM lowers di/dt. The output stage sources and sinks up to 1.5 A to drive the MOSFET gate directly. It works in peak or average current mode and with a constant or a follower-boost output.

An internal ramp starts at VM each cycle and rises by Vref (2.62 V) over one switching period; the on time ends when the ramp meets Vref. VM therefore fixes the off-time fraction, and VM is made to follow the low-frequency inductor current, so the input looks like a resistor. Without a capacitor on VM the switching ripple of the inductor current reaches the comparator and the chip behaves as a peak current-mode controller with less accurate duty; a capacitor CM on pin 5 removes that ripple and gives average current mode. CM is usually larger than Cfilter, because the differential inductance of the EMI filter helps Cfilter.

IFB = Vout/RFB is compared with Iref (200 µA typ). Below 96% of Iref the regulation output is at its top, Icontrol is fixed at Iref/2 = 100 µA and the stage is a follower boost: Vout rises with line voltage and falls as load rises. Between 96% and 100% of Iref, Icontrol falls linearly with IFB and the output is held in a narrow band (constant output voltage mode). Above Iref, Icontrol is zero, VM goes to its maximum and the on time is zero, so Vout falls back into one of the other regions.

With Icontrol constant the output voltage is proportional to Vac / Pout. A lower output at low line or heavy load shortens the on time, which lowers MOSFET and inductor losses and lets smaller, cheaper parts be used. Vout always stays above the peak input voltage, as in any boost. RM sets the maximum input power and so decides which mode the stage runs in.

When IFB exceeds 107% of Iref (Vout > 107% of RFB·Iref) Drv is held low; switching restarts by itself once IFB drops back below that level. The OVP threshold is at most 230 µA: with RFB = 1.92 MΩ and a worst-case VFB1 of 2.5 V the output can reach 444.1 V, so a 450 V output capacitor is recommended.

When IFB is below 8% of Iref the chip shuts down and draws under 50 µA; it restarts when IFB rises above 12% of Iref. In a working boost the output is always above the input, so IFB stays above both levels. UVP therefore acts when the output is abnormally low, when FB is left open, or when FB is pulled low on purpose as a shutdown input.
There is no drive while Vcontrol is 0 V. The capacitor on Vcontrol charges gradually through the internal 300 kΩ, so the duty ratio ramps up at start-up.

A resistor RCS in the return path carries the inductor current; a resistor RS from its far end to CS converts its voltage into the current IS, since the chip holds CS near 0 V. Few parts are needed and RCS also limits inrush current. IS feeds the modulator, overpower limitation and overcurrent protection.
When IS exceeds IS(OCP) (200 µA typ) Drv goes low; switching resumes once the inductor current is back below the limit. The limit is IL(OCP) = (RS/RCS) × 200 µA.

Rvac from the rectified bus feeds In. The internal mirror has about 4 V offset at its input, and a capacitor Cvac on In holds the pin at the peak of the rectified sine, since the pin draws very little current; Ivac then stands for the RMS line voltage. The pin has a 9 V ESD zener inside the chip, so Rvac should be at least 938 kΩ for instantaneous input up to 400 V.

IS·Ivac approximates the input power. When the product exceeds 3 nA², the regulation output is pulled to 0 V, which drives Vcontrol to 0 V and VM to its maximum, cutting the duty ratio toward zero. The limit releases when the product falls below 3 nA².

Place a capacitor of 1 nF to 100 nF close to the VCC pin. When the stage runs as a follower boost its output is not held at one level, so taking bias from an extra winding of the boost inductor is not recommended; VCC should come from the second-stage converter. When the output is held constant an extra inductor winding can supply VCC through two stacked capacitors, one charged to n×Vin and the other to n×(Vout - Vin), whose sum n×Vout is steady.

With no feedback current the VCC start-up current is at most 50 µA. With feedback current present and VCC below about 4 V it can rise to 1.5 mA. A PNP transistor that shunts FB to ground while VCC is low keeps the start-up draw small, so the VCC capacitor charges fast and the PFC stage starts without the second-stage converter.

The chip starts when VCC exceeds 13.25 V typ and stops when it falls below 8.7 V typ. An 18 V ESD zener inside the chip on VCC guards against excess supply voltage. After start-up the operating range is 8.7 V to 18 V.
Above 150 °C junction temperature the gate drive is disabled and the MOSFET held off; drive returns when the junction cools to about 120 °C (30 °C hysteresis).
Drv drives a power MOSFET directly with up to ±1.5 A peak current; rise and fall times are 88 ns and 61.5 ns typ into 2.2 nF.
In the 300 W, 100 kHz application circuit the power factor is 0.988 to 0.998 at 110 V input and 0.920 to 0.989 at 220 V over 67 W to 331 W input; THD is 4% to 15% and efficiency 91% to 95%.
